contradicting_evidence: Both BTC and ETH have negative order-book and taker imbalances in the Binance snapshot, providing a coherent near-term downside alternative.
The Top-100 proxy has 67% advancers, while BTC and ETH are positive over 24h; participation could support further upside instead of indecision.
frozen_forecast.expected_path: Uneven consolidation or a modest directional attempt without a defensible net-direction edge. Immediate selling pressure could produce a retest, but the supplied evidence does not establish that the positive 24h participation has failed.
falsification_conditions: Repeated completed-hour advances accompanied by persistent taker buying, stronger bid support and maintained participation would establish an upside edge.
Persistent price declines accompanied by weakening participation and sustained sell-side flow would establish a downside edge.
Strengthening ETH/BTC alongside repeated large- and mid-alt outperformance would invalidate the present weak-transmission assessment.
missing_evidence: Persistence of the observed order-book and taker imbalances is unknown.
There is no intraday breadth sequence or volume baseline with which to confirm a breakout, breakdown or absorption.
The latest settled ETF session does not measure flow during the forecast window.
supporting_evidence: BTC and ETH fell only about 0.03% in the completed hour, while ETH/BTC was unchanged. This is neither confirmed continuation nor recovery.
Positive 24h breadth conflicts with negative immediate order flow: hourly taker-buy shares were approximately 45.7% for BTC and 42.3% for ETH.
BTC open interest increased only about 0.045% as price slipped, while ETH open interest fell about 0.154%. These small changes do not establish a decisive leverage-driven move.
Transmission is uneven: approximately 59.1% of mid-alt constituents outperformed BTC, versus 41.2% of large alts and 48.9% of the Top-100 tail.
